> **What this case shows** — the [phase-lag index](../eeg-pli-alpha-eegmmidb/index.qmd) is
> volume-conduction-robust, but it — like coherence — has a *positive bias* for finite data:
> even **independent** signals produce a small spurious connectivity. The **weighted phase-lag
> index** (Vinck 2011) fixes both problems and is the recommended modern EEG connectivity
> measure: built from the imaginary cross-spectrum (so it discounts zero-lag / volume
> conduction) **and debiased** (so it removes the sample-size bias). This case validates both.
> On the same O1-Oz pair, the debiased wPLI is just **0.011** — confirming (like the PLI 0.016)
> that the strong alpha PLV of 0.92 is mostly volume conduction. And the debiasing works: for
> constructed **independent** signals the biased wPLI is a spurious **0.038** but the debiased
> wPLI collapses to **0.0006**, while genuine lagged coupling keeps a debiased wPLI of **1.0**.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for the state-of-the-art connectivity value: `weightedPLI(x, y, sr, freq_band,
debiased = TRUE)` → read `wpli_debiased`.
**Way of thinking** — the biased wPLI/PLI/coherence all inflate for short data; the *debiased*
wPLI is unbiased (it can even go slightly negative for uncoupled signals). Prefer it.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioCrossModal::weightedPLI()`; compare with `phaseLagIndex()` and
`phaseLockingValue()` to complete the picture.
:::

## Proposition

On real O1-Oz alpha, the debiased wPLI is low (0.011), `weightedPLI` reproduces an independent
scipy imaginary-cross-spectrum wPLI (~7e-3), and its debiasing removes spurious connectivity
(independent → biased 0.038 / debiased 0.0006; lagged → debiased 1.0).

## Question & goal

**The question is whether the debiased wPLI does what it promises: discount volume conduction
AND remove the finite-sample bias — and whether the ecosystem computes it correctly.** The goal
is to validate `weightedPLI` against scipy and to demonstrate the debiasing on signals with a
known coupling type.

## Challenge & approach

wPLI is built from the imaginary cross-spectrum Im(analytic_x · conj(analytic_y)); the debiased
form (Vinck Eq. 6) subtracts the diagonal terms. We compute it with `weightedPLI`, re-compute
it with scipy, and run it on constructed independent / lagged / zero-lag signals.

```
O1, Oz EEG → weightedPLI(alpha, debiased) → wPLI = 0.113, debiased = 0.011
                    vs scipy (Im cross-spectrum, Vinck Eq. 6)   → agreement (~7e-3)
                    vs independent / lagged signals              → debiasing: 0.038 -> 0.0006 ; lagged 1.0
```

## Data

**eegmmidb (PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02 (eyes-closed)**, occipital **O1** and
**Oz**, 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked pair the PLV and PLI cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the debiasing. For INDEPENDENT signals the biased wPLI (orange) is a spurious 0.04, but the debiased wPLI (green) collapses to ~0 — the finite-sample bias removed; for genuinely lagged coupling both stay at 1.0; for zero-lag (volume conduction) both are ~0. Right: the real O1-Oz alpha across the connectivity family — PLV (0.92) counts volume conduction, while PLI (0.02), wPLI (0.11) and especially the debiased wPLI (0.01) all discount it, agreeing the genuine lagged coupling is minimal.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* the left panel shows *why* the debiased wPLI is trusted (it removes spurious
connectivity); the right panel completes the PLV → PLI → wPLI story on real data.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| real O1-Oz wPLI (biased) | **0.113** |
| real O1-Oz **debiased wPLI** | **0.011** |
| independent — biased wPLI (spurious) | 0.038 |
| independent — **debiased wPLI (corrected)** | **0.0006** |
| lagged — debiased wPLI (genuine) | 1.00 |
| wPLI vs scipy (max \|diff\|) | 7e-3 |

The debiasing works, the op matches scipy, and the real occipital alpha coupling is minimal once
volume conduction and bias are removed. Values trace to
[`artifacts/wpli_summary.csv`](artifacts/wpli_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

The debiased weighted phase-lag index is the connectivity measure to reach for: it discounts
volume conduction *and* removes the finite-sample bias, and on real occipital EEG it confirms
that a headline alpha PLV of 0.92 reflects almost no genuine lagged coupling. The transferable
takeaway: **default to the debiased wPLI for phase connectivity; a biased measure (PLI,
coherence, PLV) can show spurious coupling on short data — the debiased wPLI won't — and a
low debiased wPLI is a conservative lower bound on genuine lagged interaction.**

## Open questions

- This completes the canonical phase-connectivity trio on one pair (**PLV** volume-conduction-
  *sensitive*; **PLI** and **debiased wPLI** volume-conduction-*robust*). The natural next step
  is a full channel × channel debiased-wPLI matrix — the genuinely-lagged posterior alpha
  network — and a contrast of that network eyes-closed vs eyes-open. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| debiased weighted PLI (the standard) | `weightedPLI(debiased = TRUE)` | PhysioCrossModal |
| phase-lag index (biased, VC-robust) | `phaseLagIndex()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| phase-locking value (VC-sensitive) | `phaseLockingValue()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| magnitude-squared coherence | `coherence()` | PhysioCrossModal |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **debiased** — keep `TRUE` (the default): the debiased estimator is unbiased for finite data;
  the biased wPLI over-reports connectivity on short segments.
- **freq_band** — the band to test (here `c(8, 13)`, alpha).
- **reading a value** — a low debiased wPLI means little *lagged* coupling; it does not rule out
  genuine zero-lag interaction (which wPLI, being VC-robust, also discounts).

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioCrossModal)

w <- weightedPLI(o1, oz, sr = 160, freq_band = c(8, 13), debiased = TRUE)
w$wpli_debiased   # 0.011 -- little genuine lagged alpha coupling (mostly volume conduction)

# reproduces an independent scipy imaginary-cross-spectrum wPLI (~7e-3); debiasing verified.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/`](artifacts/) — the summary in
[`wpli_summary.csv`](artifacts/wpli_summary.csv) — and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks each
number, the scipy agreement, the debiasing demonstration, and the honestly-noted filtfilt and
conservativeness caveats.
